user_decision.question: Phase 11.20's register discriminator is measured on both sides and the two sides disagree: the iterated splice delivers only a Drift-distance bound that grows with the copy index (register_interior_displacement_bound_at_block) and REFUTES kappa's clipped/residue register reading at the window's interior (iterSpliced_register_clipped_interior_refuted, at every Tn >= 3 and every P), while the stab-bit agreement REFUTES both the Drift-distance reading and dropping the register conjunct (stab_bit_ne_of_register_ne) and consumes only the clipped reading (stab_alphaR_eq_of_clipped_eq). So no position-pair relation carrying a register conjunct exists for the depth induction. Which route should the plan be revised onto?
options: (B-1) Restrict the pump's block selection to blocks across which the original's register is already nearly constant, so side (A)'s Drift obstruction is hypothesised away rather than argued around. Cost: a new block-selection condition on top of exists_typeBlock_of_spacing, and nothing landed says such blocks exist at the needed spacing -- a research round would be owed first.

(B-2) Move the register bridging off the path level entirely, onto the certificate side, so no position-pair relation carries a register conjunct at all. Cost: the transport the depth induction consumes would then not be a path-level correspondence, which re-opens the shape of Phases 11.21 and 11.6.

(B-3) Abandon the depth-stratified path-level route for this task and mark the realization theorem [BLOCKED] whole on the register coordinate, keeping the two compiled measurements as the recorded obstruction.
user_decision.recommendation: (B-1), but only after a research round: the obstruction is specifically a CLIMBING register across the block, and the pump's blocks come from a pigeonhole over (object, type) pairs that says nothing about the register, so whether blocks with a near-constant register exist at spacing P+1 is a measurable question rather than an open-ended one. (B-2) discards the position-pair correspondence the whole stratification was built to supply.
user_decision.why_user: This is a route decision with a large and NOT COSTABLE scope difference between the options, and it lifts or discards work already landed in Phases 11.18 through 11.20; the artifacts cannot infer which cost the user is willing to pay. It is a NEW, second obstruction that route (W-2) left unaddressed -- (W-2) authorised weakening the register conjunct to whatever the pump's pairs satisfy, and the measurement now shows that what they satisfy is strictly weaker than what the bit needs -- so the original question is not re-asked.
